question.problem:
The parabola $y=-{x}^{2}-4x$ and the line $y=4$ intersect at the point $P.$ Find the coordinates of $P.$

The coordinates of $P$ are
$(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=-{x}^{2}-4x \\ y=4\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-4x & =4 \\ -{x}^{2}-4x-4 & =0 \\ -({x}^{2}+4x+4) & =0 \\ -(x+2)(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point is $x=-2.$

We know the y-coordinate of the intersection point from the equation of the line. So, the only point of intersection is $(-2,4).$
